children: will spend more than $230M on Whole Foods employees by raising the hourly pay and offering benefits to the grocery chain’s 100K team members.
This marks the most significant investment in Whole Foods employees to date.
On September 28, U.S. Whole Foods’ hourly employees will see their pay rise to $21 an hour and to $29 per hour (on average) when including the value of their elected benefits.

These benefits will be available beginning January 1, 2027, when eligible team members gain access to health, family, and financial support benefits for as little as $5 per week. Coverage also includes company-paid short- and long-term disability, fertility and family-building care, and fully paid parental leave of up to 20 weeks.
Part-time employees will receive dental and vision coverage and free basic life insurance.
Later in 2027, employees will gain access to prepaid college tuition, skills training, and certifications.
While the company made no mention of unionization efforts at the grocery chain, the pay hike/benefits come after the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) rejected Amazon’s

petition to throw out a recent union vote. Management claims United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) interfered with a union vote and that federal restrictions against mandatory corporate "captive audience" anti-union meetings violated management’s free speech.
The NLRB ruled against Whole Foods management and upheld the union’s certification, forcing the company to negotiate with union representatives.

title: Amazon investing $230M in higher pay, benefits for Whole Foods employees
